requirement_text.REQ-365: Per explicit user decision: platform-level help (shared screens like login-routing that no tenant owns) is authored through the BA-agent/REQ-ANALYST pipeline, matching the exact platform-vs-tenant split already established for UAT scenarios (REQ-358's scope field, REQ-359's BA-persona/REQ-ANALYST split, REQ-360's login-routing scenario as the worked platform example). This requirement is the authoring-path equivalent for help content: it does not re-derive that split, it applies it. . SCOPE: wherever REQ-363's design placed platform-scope help content (a dedicated table/schema, per that requirement's own acceptance criterion), this requirement adds the write path/tooling REQ-ANALYST (or, once REQ-359 lands, whichever role it specifies for platform content) actually uses to author it — this could be as simple as a direct context-module call analogous to REQ-364's tenant-scoped one, scoped to the platform table instead, reusing REQ-364's create/update/publish/reconfirm shape rather than inventing a parallel one. Explicitly NOT a new UI — platform help authoring is agent-pipeline-driven, matching how platform-scope UAT scenarios are authored (a file/record written by an agent, not a form filled by a human). . FIRST REAL CONTENT: author help for the login-routing screen (the same screen REQ-360's UAT scenario covers) as this requirement's own worked, real example — proves the authoring path end-to-end rather than shipping an authoring mechanism with zero real content using it.

task.description: On branch feature/WF02-REQ365-20260918. Read lib/letflow/design/req365-platform-help-authoring.md independently (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary). Specifically verify: (a) the platform_help_content migration shape is fully specified and consistent with req363 design §3 (public schema, no prefix, no tenant_scoped_migrations registration); (b) the write-path module/function shapes are complete and consistent with lib/letflow/help.ex's actual shipped signatures (read that file, don't take the design doc's word for it); (c) the sanitization-reuse mechanism is concretely specified, not hand-waved; (d) the literal login-routing help content text is genuinely present, in plain end-user language, and the screen_id is stated explicitly. FAIL immediately on any check failure, no partial credit — list every failed check by requirement id. On PASS, complete the handoff (status COMPLETED, result.status PASS, next_action "Route to ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a)"), commit and push to feature/WF02-REQ365-20260918. On FAIL, complete the handoff with result.status FAIL and next_action "Rework CODE-DESIGNER", listing every failed check.

result.summary: REQ-365 design (lib/letflow/design/req365-platform-help-authoring.md) read in full, independently, alongside req363's design, lib/letflow/help.ex, and lib/letflow/help/help_content.ex (also read in full, not taken on the design doc's word). Checks (a), (c), (d) pass. Check (b) fails: three of the six Letflow.Help.Platform function signatures in §3.2 (publish/1, reconfirm/1, withdraw/1) are NOT consistent with the actual shipped Letflow.Help error unions they claim to mirror, and the design gives no rationale for the specific divergence found (unlike its own, explicitly-reasoned omission of :invalid_prefix in §3.1). FAILING immediately per WF-02 Step 1b's no-partial-credit rule.

a_migration_shape.detail: Design §1.3 specifies platform_help_content as an unguarded, unregistered, non-prefixed migration (no `if prefix() do`, no `prefix:` on create table/indexes, not added to Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0), matching req363 design §3's placement decision exactly and mirroring the real 20260816000001_create_tenants.exs / 20260816000004_create_users.exs shape cited in §0.

b_write_path_signatures.detail: lib/letflow/help.ex (read in full) shows publish/2, reconfirm/2, and withdraw/2 all declare {:error, Ecto.Changeset.t()} in their @spec error unions (lines 130-136, 163-169, 195-200) — consistent with each function's own Repo.update/2 call, whose own return type is {:ok, struct} | {:error, Ecto.Changeset.t()} regardless of whether the changeset was built via Ecto.Changeset.change/2 (no validations) or a full changeset function. The REQ-365 design's §3.2 Letflow.Help.Platform.publish/1 (lines 286-288), .reconfirm/1 (lines 292-294), and .withdraw/1 (lines 298-300) all OMIT {:error, Ecto.Changeset.t()} from their @spec, with no stated reason. This is a real, checkable inconsistency between the design and the shipped module it claims to mirror "exactly" (design §0: 'reuses their exact calling convention... error-tuple vocabulary'). Contrast with §3.1's explicit, reasoned justification for dropping :invalid_prefix (no prefix concept exists for this table) — that omission is argued; the {:error, Ecto.Changeset.t()} omission for these three functions is not argued anywhere in the document, and nothing in §3.3's process_definition_id reasoning explains it either (§3.3 only removes the resolve_confirmed_version/2 branch, it says nothing about why Repo.update's own changeset-error case would become unreachable). create_draft/1 and update_draft/2 correctly retain {:error, Ecto.Changeset.t()} in their own specs (§3.2 lines 259-264, 274-279), which makes the omission on the other three functions look like an oversight rather than a considered scope narrowing — exactly the kind of incompletely-specified error shape Step 1b's check (b)/(c) exists to catch before ELIXIR-DEV builds against it.

c_sanitization_reuse.detail: Design §5 concretely specifies extraction of help_content.ex's existing private validate_markdown_safety/2 and its full call graph (walk/1, walk_node/1, walk_text/1, flatten_plain_text/1, raw_html_node?/2, destination_violation/2, scheme_violation_for/2, unsafe_scheme?/1, scheme_letters/1, decode_numeric_entities/1, decode_entity_code/1, codepoint_to_binary/2, safe_codepoint/1, plus the three module attributes) into a new Letflow.Help.MarkdownSafety module exposing one public validate(changeset, field) function, called from both HelpContent and PlatformHelpContent's changesets. Not hand-waved — names the exact functions moving, the one new public surface, and states no new dependency is introduced.

d_login_routing_content.detail: Design §4.1 states screen_id explicitly as "login-routing", with reasoning tracing it to the requirement text and REQ-360's shipped UAT scenario id. §4.2 contains literal, complete title ("Signing in and where you land") and full markdown body in plain end-user language (no SHALL-statement/engineer prose) — genuinely present, not a placeholder or TBD.
